nodes.name: Carbon black acid treatment
nodes.procedure: Commercial carbon black (Ketjenblack, EC-300J) was first mixed with 100 ml of 70 wt% HNO3 and continuously stirred under reflux in a preheated oil bath at 70°C for 2 h. The mixture was then filtered and rinsed with DI water and ethanol until the filtrate was neutral. The resulting powder was dried overnight in a vacuum oven at 60°C.

nodes.name: Pt/C synthesis
nodes.procedure: 300 mg of the treated carbon was ultrasonically mixed with 200 ml ethylene glycol and 100 ml DI water in a round-bottomed flask to obtain a homogeneous solution. Then, 1.35 ml of a 0.25M H2PtCl6 aqueous solution was added and the mixture stirred at room temperature for 18 h and then in an oil bath at 120°C for 2 h. The resulting catalyst was filtered and washed with DI water and ethanol to remove unreacted monomer and other residues and then dried under vacuum at 60°C.

nodes.name: MoO3-x@Pt/C impregnation
nodes.procedure: 100 mg of the presynthesized Pt/C catalyst and 1.85 g (NH4)6Mo7O24·6H2O were added to a mixture of 100 ml ethanol and water (1:3, v/v) in a round-bottomed flask and sonicated for 30 min, followed by magnetic stirring to obtain a well-dispersed slurry. The sample was then filtered and dried under vacuum at 60°C.

nodes.procedure: The dried sample was reduced under a H2/N2 (10:90, v/v) atmosphere in a furnace at 500°C for 4 h to obtain the MoO3-x@Pt/C catalyst.

nodes.evidence_snippet: As illustrated in Fig. 2c, the intensity of the characteristic O–H stretching vibrations of H2O molecules (3,000-3,750 cm−1) increases with increasing cathode potential; similarly, the Mo–O–H signals also intensify... H3O+ bands are clearly observed at ~1,800 cm−1.

nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) showed substantial loss of the C 1s and F 1s signals from the MEA of the Pt/C||IrO2 electrolyser after operation compared with the pristine MEA, while... no obvious changes in the XPS C 1s and F 1s signals were observed in the MEA of the MoO3−x@Pt/C||IrO2 electrolyser.
